headline: The Roadside Help & Mechanics Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can brief and coach travel companions on breakdown safety, negotiate hidden faults and substitute cars with mechanics and rental agents, refuse unsafe help, report incidents to police and emergency services, and document a hard breakdown day in writing and by phone in Spanish.

lessons.title: Brief Your Co-Driver Before the Mountain Pass
lessons.objective: Explain in order, with reasons, what your group does if the car fails on a mountain pass.

words.note: Argentina: poner las balizas. In Mexico you hear luces intermitentes.
Argentina. In Mexico it is el acotamiento.
Argentina and Chile for gravel road surface.
Argentina. In Mexico it is la llanta de refacción.
Argentina. Elsewhere el extintor.
Argentina prefers tránsito over tráfico.

words.en: First we turn on the hazard lights and then we stop on the shoulder.
words.es: Primero ponemos las balizas y después paramos en la banquina.

words.en: We get out on the right, because cars pass on the left.
words.es: Bajamos por la derecha, porque los autos pasan por la izquierda.

words.en: We set the parking brake because on the downhill the car rolls.
words.es: Ponemos el freno de mano porque en la bajada el auto rueda.

words.en: There's no coverage on the cliff stretch; that's why we tell someone before going up.
words.es: No hay cobertura en la cornisa; por eso avisamos antes de subir.

words.en: Meanwhile, we wait behind the guardrail, never next to the car.
words.es: Mientras tanto, esperamos detrás del guardarraíl, nunca al lado del auto.

words.en: Do you get why that comes first?
words.note: Informal, Argentine voseo: entendés instead of entiendes.

words.en: If there's smoke, first we move away and then we call.
words.es: Si sale humo, primero nos alejamos y después llamamos.

words.en: Good afternoon, we're stranded on Route 33, Cuesta del Obispo.
words.es: Buenas tardes, estamos varados en la Ruta 33, Cuesta del Obispo.
words.note: Formal, for the emergency or assistance line.

lessons.speaking: You are briefing the AI, your travel buddy Tomás Arias, on the breakdown plan for the Cuesta del Obispo: explain each step in order and why it comes first, using primero, luego, después, porque and por eso.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero ponemos las balizas, luego salimos por la derecha, porque..., por eso...)

examples.es: Primero ponemos las balizas y luego salimos por la derecha.
examples.en: First we turn on the hazard lights and then we get out on the right.

examples.es: El matafuegos va adelante porque lo necesitamos rápido.
examples.en: The fire extinguisher goes up front because we need it fast.

lessons.title: Explain the Rental's Roadside Coverage Back to the Agent
lessons.objective: Read the roadside-assistance clause and explain back what is covered, what is not, and what to do first.

words.note: Same form in singular and plural: el parabrisas, los parabrisas.
Costa Rica: lastre means gravel.
Agrees with the noun: las llantas no están cubiertas.

words.en: Let me explain it back in my own words to see if I understood.
words.es: Déjeme explicárselo con mis palabras, a ver si entendí.
words.note: Formal, to the agent.

words.en: If I understand correctly, you call the assistance line first.
words.es: Si entiendo bien, primero se llama a la línea de asistencia.

words.en: So if the windshield breaks, do you pay the deductible?
words.es: Entonces, si se rompe el parabrisas, ¿se paga el deducible?

words.en: It says here that tires and glass require the extra insurance.
words.es: Aquí dice que llantas y vidrios requieren el seguro adicional.

words.en: Can you show me where that exclusion is in the contract?
words.es: ¿Me puede mostrar dónde está esa exclusión en el contrato?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: What do you do first if the car won't start?
words.es: ¿Qué se hace primero si el carro no arranca?

words.en: If you drive on a gravel road, do you lose the coverage?
words.es: Si se maneja por un camino de lastre, ¿se pierde la cobertura?

words.en: Heads up, the tires aren't covered without the insurance.
words.es: Ojo, las llantas no están cubiertas sin el seguro.
words.note: Informal, to your travel partner.

lessons.speaking: You are the renter, and the AI is Mariela Solís, the rental agent at Liberia airport: read the roadside-assistance clause with her and explain it back, saying what is covered, what is not and what to do first, using se llama, se cubre and si + present.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se llama primero a asistencia; si se pincha una llanta, no se cubre...)

examples.es: Se llama primero a la línea de asistencia y luego se espera en un lugar seguro.
examples.en: You call the assistance line first and then you wait in a safe place.

examples.es: Si se pincha una llanta, no se cubre sin el seguro adicional.
examples.en: If a tire goes flat, it isn't covered without the extra insurance.

lessons.title: Coach Your Niece Through a Tire Pressure Check
lessons.objective: Coach a companion step by step through a tire pressure check and have her teach it back to you.

words.note: Spain says pegatina; in Mexico you hear calcomanía.
Spain: neumáticos or ruedas, not llantas.
Spain uses ordenador; Latin America says computadora.

words.en: Take the cap off the valve and keep it in your pocket.
words.es: Quítale el tapón a la válvula y guárdalo en el bolsillo.
words.note: Informal tú, to your niece.

words.en: Look at the door-jamb label; that's the recommended pressure.
words.es: Mira la pegatina de la puerta; esa es la presión recomendada.

words.en: Put it on straight; if you hear a hiss, it's not on right.
words.es: Ponla recta; si oyes un silbido, no está bien puesta.

words.en: Don't lose it; without a cap, dirt gets into the valve.
words.es: No lo pierdas; sin tapón entra suciedad en la válvula.

words.en: The gauge and the display don't match; let's check it again.
words.es: El manómetro y la pantalla no coinciden; vamos a comprobarlo otra vez.

words.en: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso a paso.

words.en: Very good, you did it perfectly.
words.es: Muy bien, lo has hecho perfecto.
words.note: Spain uses the present perfect for something just finished.

words.en: Excuse me, is there another gauge to compare?
words.note: Formal, to the station attendant.

lessons.speaking: You are coaching the AI, your 17-year-old niece Valentina, through a tire pressure check at a gas station near Zaragoza: give step-by-step commands like quítale el tapón, revísala en frío and no lo pierdas, then have her teach it back to you.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (quítale el tapón, revísala en frío, no lo pierdas)

examples.es: Quítale el tapón y no lo pierdas.
examples.en: Take the cap off and don't lose it.

examples.es: Compruébalas en frío y compáralas con la pegatina de la puerta.
examples.en: Check them cold and compare them with the door-jamb label.

lessons.title: Read the Scooter Checklist Before Riding Off
lessons.objective: Read a scooter rental's pre-ride checklist and explain which checks come before leaving and which one failed.

words.note: Mexico: palomita is a tick; palomear means to tick off.
Agrees with the noun: la palanca está floja.
Mexico. In Spain you hear intermitentes.

words.en: Before leaving, we have to test both brakes.
words.es: Antes de salir hay que probar los dos frenos.

words.en: This box is already ticked, but the rear lever is loose.
words.es: Esta casilla ya tiene palomita, pero la palanca trasera está floja.

words.en: Could you adjust it for me before I sign, please?
words.es: ¿Me la puede ajustar antes de firmar, por favor?
words.note: Formal usted, to the attendant.

words.en: I won't sign until the brake is firm.
words.es: No firmo hasta que el freno quede firme.

words.en: Camila, squeeze your lever; does it feel the same as mine?
words.es: Camila, aprieta tu palanca; ¿la sientes igual que la mía?
words.note: Informal tú, to your riding partner.

words.en: After adjusting it, we have to test it again.
words.es: Después de ajustarla, hay que probarla otra vez.

words.en: If it can't be fixed, can you give me another scooter?
words.es: Si no se puede arreglar, ¿me puede dar otra motoneta?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: We need to take photos of the scratches before leaving.
words.es: Hay que tomar fotos de los rayones antes de salir.

lessons.speaking: You are the renter, and the AI is Rubén Cruz, the attendant at a scooter rental in Puerto Escondido: read the pre-ride checklist with him and your partner Camila, and explain which checks come before leaving, using antes de, después de and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de salir hay que probar los frenos; después de firmar...)

examples.es: Antes de salir hay que probar el freno trasero.
examples.en: Before leaving, you have to test the rear brake.

examples.es: Después de ponernos el casco, hay que revisar las direccionales.
examples.en: After putting on our helmets, we have to check the turn signals.

lessons.title: Mechanic Calls: Cracked Hose Found During a Tire Repair
lessons.objective: Recount what the car was doing, understand the new fault, and propose how to proceed and who authorizes it.

words.note: Common in Ecuador for a small tire repair shop.
Used in Ecuador; Mexico says la refacción.
Common in Ecuador for the car rental company.

words.en: Yesterday, when we drove up to El Cajas, the needle was slowly rising.
words.es: Ayer, cuando subimos al Cajas, la aguja subía poco a poco.
words.note: Preterite for the event, imperfect for what was going on.

words.en: We stopped for 10 minutes and then the temperature went back to normal.
words.es: Paramos 10 minutos y después la temperatura volvió a lo normal.

words.en: Is the crack in the lower hose or near the clamp?
words.es: ¿La grieta está en la manguera inferior o cerca de la abrazadera?

words.en: I'd rather call the rental company before authorizing anything.
words.es: Yo preferiría llamar a la rentadora antes de autorizar nada.
words.note: Formal, to the mechanic.

words.en: How much would the part cost, labor included?
words.es: ¿Cuánto costaría el repuesto, con la mano de obra incluida?

words.en: Could you send me a photo of the crack on WhatsApp?
words.es: ¿Podría mandarme una foto de la grieta por WhatsApp?
words.note: Formal usted.

words.en: I'll let you know as soon as the rental company gives me the go-ahead.
words.es: Le aviso en cuanto la rentadora me dé el visto bueno.

words.en: Hey, do you remember the needle was rising yesterday?
words.es: Oye, ¿te acuerdas de que ayer la aguja subía?
words.note: Informal tú, to your travel companion.

lessons.speaking: You are the driver of the rental car, and the AI is Don Hernán, the mechanic in Cuenca, calling about your car: recount what the temperature gauge did yesterday using the preterite and imperfect, ask about the new fault, and propose next steps with yo preferiría and sería mejor.

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (la aguja subía cuando subimos la cuesta; yo preferiría llamar primero a la rentadora)

examples.es: Mientras subíamos al Cajas, la aguja llegó casi a la zona roja.
examples.en: While we were climbing to El Cajas, the needle almost reached the red zone.

examples.es: Yo preferiría llamar a la rentadora antes de cambiar la manguera.
examples.en: I'd rather call the rental company before the hose gets changed.

lessons.title: Substitute Car Too Small for Five and the Luggage
lessons.objective: Compare the substitute options and negotiate what happens next and when your own car will be ready.

words.note: In Chile camioneta covers SUVs and pickups.
In Chile mecánico means manual transmission.
Chilean usage; you also hear la maleta del auto.
Common loanword in Chile.

words.en: There are 5 of us with big backpacks; we're not going to fit.
words.es: Somos 5 y llevamos mochilas grandes; no vamos a caber.

words.en: This car is smaller than the SUV we booked.
words.es: Este auto es más chico que la camioneta que reservamos.

words.en: When is the part for the SUV going to arrive?
words.es: ¿Cuándo va a llegar la pieza para la camioneta?

words.en: Do you have a van or a bigger automatic car?
words.es: ¿Tiene una van o algún auto automático más grande?
words.note: Formal, to the agent.

words.en: Does the van cost as much as the SUV, or is there a price difference?
words.es: ¿La van cuesta tanto como la camioneta, o hay diferencia de precio?

words.en: Can we swap the car at the Puerto Varas branch?
words.es: ¿Podemos cambiar el auto en la sucursal de Puerto Varas?

words.en: Guys, this car is a manual; can anyone drive stick?
words.es: Chiquillos, este auto es mecánico; ¿alguien sabe manejar con cambios?
words.note: Informal; chiquillos is Chilean for guys.

words.en: I need that in writing in the contract, please.
words.es: Necesito eso por escrito en el contrato, por favor.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler with a group of 5, and the AI is Francisca, the rental agent in Puerto Montt: compare the substitute options with más… que and tan… como, and pin down what happens next and when your SUV will be ready using the future and ir a.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (el otro va a ser más pequeño que este; la pieza llegará el martes; es tan caro como...)

examples.es: La van va a ser más cara que el auto mecánico.
examples.en: The van is going to be more expensive than the manual car.

examples.es: La pieza llegará el martes y la camioneta estará lista el miércoles.
examples.en: The part will arrive on Tuesday and the SUV will be ready on Wednesday.

lessons.title: Highway Police Stop at Your Breakdown
lessons.objective: Narrate what happened to a traffic officer and give the times, plate, road marker and document numbers clearly.

words.note: Colombian term for a traffic ticket.
Colombian short form of pase de conducción.
Colombia's required traffic insurance; officers ask to see it.
Colombian word for the road shoulder.
Colombia says la placa in the singular.
Colombian highway markers show PR plus a number.
Colombian word for a case or claim number.
Common in Colombia for a stranded car or people.

words.en: We stopped at 3:10, at marker PR 34, heading to Manizales.
words.es: Paramos a las 3:10, en el PR 34, hacia Manizales.

words.en: The car lost power on the climb and we stopped on the shoulder.
words.es: El carro perdió fuerza en la subida y paramos en la berma.

words.en: We put out the triangle and we all waited outside the car.
words.es: Pusimos el triángulo y todos esperamos fuera del carro.

words.en: The plate is KLM 482; it's a rental car.
words.es: La placa es KLM 482; es un carro de alquiler.

words.en: Here are my passport, my license and the vehicle registration.
words.es: Aquí tiene mi pasaporte, mi pase y la tarjeta de propiedad.
words.note: Formal, to the officer.

words.en: One moment, sergeant, the tow truck driver is calling me.
words.es: Un momento, sargento, me está llamando el conductor de la grúa.

words.en: The driver says he's now arriving at 4:15.
words.es: El conductor dice que ahora llega a las 4:15.

words.en: Could you give me your name for the report, please?
words.es: ¿Me regala su nombre para el reporte, por favor?
words.note: Me regala is the polite Colombian way to ask for something.

lessons.speaking: You are the driver of the broken-down rental, and the AI is Sargento Ortiz, a traffic officer: tell him what happened in the preterite (paramos, pusimos, llamamos) and give the times, plate, road marker and document numbers clearly.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (paramos a las tres y diez en el kilómetro treinta y cuatro; la placa es...)

examples.es: Salimos de Pereira a las 2:30 y paramos a las 3:10.
examples.en: We left Pereira at 2:30 and stopped at 3:10.

examples.es: Llamé a la asistencia y me dieron el radicado 58213.
examples.en: I called roadside assistance and they gave me reference number 58213.

lessons.title: Saying No to a Stranger Who Wants to Open the Radiator
lessons.objective: Politely refuse unsafe roadside help, explain why, and suggest a safer way the helper can assist.

words.note: River Plate word for a plastic jug or can.
Uruguayan term for roadside assistance.

words.en: Wait, don't open it yet, please!
words.es: ¡Espere, no lo abra todavía, por favor!
words.note: Formal usted, polite with an older stranger.

words.en: I don't recommend we touch it while it's hot; the manual says to wait.
words.es: No recomiendo que lo toquemos en caliente; el manual dice esperar.

words.en: With the pressure, the boiling water can shoot out and burn you.
words.es: Con la presión, el agua hirviendo puede salir y quemarlo.

words.en: Thank you so much for stopping; I really appreciate it.
words.es: Muchas gracias por parar; de verdad se lo agradezco.

words.en: Could you lend me your phone to call roadside assistance?
words.es: ¿Me presta su celular para llamar al auxilio mecánico?

words.en: Don't pour cold water on the engine; let's save the jug.
words.es: No tire agua fría al motor; mejor guardemos el bidón.

words.en: Don't worry, we'll wait for it to cool down and check it together.
words.es: No se preocupe, esperamos a que se enfríe y lo revisamos juntos.

words.en: Can you pass me the manual in the glove box?
words.es: ¿Me pasás el manual que está en la guantera?
words.note: Informal vos, as used in Uruguay, to your travel companion.

lessons.speaking: You are the driver of the overheated car, and the AI is Washington, a farmer who stopped to help: thank him, stop him from opening the radiator with negative commands like no lo abra todavía, explain why with no recomiendo que + subjunctive, and suggest a safer way to help.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no lo abra todavía; no recomiendo que lo toquemos en caliente, el manual dice esperar)

examples.es: No lo abra todavía; la tapa está muy caliente.
examples.en: Don't open it yet; the cap is very hot.

examples.es: No recomiendo que usted ponga la mano cerca del ventilador.
examples.en: I don't recommend that you put your hand near the fan.

lessons.title: Feedback for a Friend Who Rode the Brakes Downhill
lessons.objective: Give a friend tactful driving feedback, recommend changes, and have her explain the advice back to you.

words.note: Spain: reducir una marcha = to shift down a gear.
Spain usage; Mexico says el acotamiento.
Frenar a toques = to brake in short presses, not continuously.
Feminine form, for Nerea; tranquilo for a man.

words.en: Nerea, I'm not saying it to criticize you, honestly.
words.es: Nerea, no te lo digo para criticarte, de verdad.
words.note: Informal: in Spain friends use tú.

words.en: I recommend you use a low gear, as the manual says.
words.es: Te recomiendo que uses una marcha corta, como dice el manual.

words.en: I'd rather we wait here until the brakes cool down.
words.es: Prefiero que esperemos aquí hasta que se enfríen los frenos.
words.note: Hasta que + subjunctive for something that hasn't happened yet.

words.en: I suggest you brake in short presses, not the whole time.
words.es: Te sugiero que frenes a toques, no todo el rato.

words.en: I hope the rest of the descent is calmer.
words.es: Ojalá que el resto del descenso sea más tranquilo.

words.en: It happened to me too the first time I drove down a pass.
words.es: A mí también me pasó la primera vez que bajé un puerto.

words.en: Can you explain it to me in your own words?
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend.

lessons.speaking: You are Nerea's friend at a lookout below Teide, and the AI is Nerea, who rode the brakes downhill and feels defensive: give tactful feedback with te recomiendo que and ojalá que plus the subjunctive, then have her explain the advice back to you.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (te recomiendo que uses una marcha más corta, como dijo el mecánico; ojalá que...)

examples.es: Te recomiendo que reduzcas antes de cada curva.
examples.en: I recommend you shift down before each bend.

examples.es: Ojalá que no tengas que pisar tanto el freno.
examples.en: I hope you don't have to press the brake so much.

lessons.title: Settle a Dispute Over What the Mechanic Said
lessons.objective: Report what each person heard the mechanic say, settle the disagreement, and confirm with the mechanic.

words.note: Estar en condiciones = to be in good enough shape to use.

words.en: Andrés says Don Efraín said the car was fit to drive.
words.es: Andrés dice que Don Efraín dijo que el carro estaba en condiciones.
words.note: Don + first name is a respectful title for an older man.

words.en: Sofía understood that we could only drive short distances.
words.es: Sofía entendió que solo podíamos manejar distancias cortas.

words.en: While he was talking, the compressor was making a lot of noise.
words.es: Cuando él hablaba, el compresor hacía mucho ruido.

words.en: You're both partly right; let's just ask him again.
words.es: Los dos tienen algo de razón; mejor le preguntamos otra vez.
words.note: Informal, to both friends.

words.en: Don Efraín, did you say the car could go out on the highway?
words.es: Don Efraín, ¿usted dijo que el carro podía salir a carretera?
words.note: Formal: usted with the mechanic.

words.en: Could you repeat it to us slowly, please?
words.es: ¿Nos lo puede repetir despacio, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: So you're saying it's a temporary fix, right?
words.es: Entonces usted dice que es un arreglo provisional, ¿verdad?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Nobody meant any harm; it was just a misunderstanding.
words.es: Nadie tenía mala intención; solo hubo un malentendido.

lessons.speaking: You are the friend in the middle at a café in Antigua, and the AI plays Andrés, Sofía and then mechanic Don Efraín: report each version with dice que and dijo que, use the imperfect for the background, and confirm with usted what the mechanic really said.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Andrés dice que el mecánico dijo que podíamos seguir; cuando hablaba, había mucho ruido)

examples.es: Sofía dijo que el mecánico quería revisar los frenos otra vez.
examples.en: Sofía said the mechanic wanted to check the brakes again.

examples.es: Cuando Don Efraín explicaba, nosotros estábamos afuera.
examples.en: When Don Efraín was explaining, we were outside.

lessons.title: Keep Your In-Laws Going Through a Long Garage Wait
lessons.objective: Encourage a tired group, commit to concrete next steps, and keep spirits up during a long wait.

words.note: In Argentina, parts often travel by encomienda on long-distance buses.
Argentina usage.
Popular Argentine card game; good for passing time with family.
Argentina usage: a booked car with driver, common in small towns.

words.en: I'll call the garage every hour and tell you what they say.
words.es: Llamaré al taller cada hora y les contaré qué dicen.

words.en: Don't worry, we'll find an open diner.
words.es: No se preocupen, conseguiremos un comedor abierto.

words.en: Hang in there, it won't be long now!
Bruno, if you behave, we'll go to the kiosk later.
words.es: Bruno, si te portás bien, después iremos al kiosco.
words.note: Informal vos with the child: portás, not portas.

words.en: Ramiro, I'll take care of picking up the parcel at the bus station.
words.es: Ramiro, yo me encargaré de buscar la encomienda en la terminal.
words.note: Respectful tone with your father-in-law.

words.en: If the part doesn't arrive today, we'll look for lodging in town.
words.es: Si la pieza no llega hoy, buscaremos hospedaje en el pueblo.

words.en: Elena, thank you for your patience; I know it's a long day.
words.es: Elena, gracias por la paciencia; sé que es un día largo.
words.note: Respectful tone with your mother-in-law.

words.en: Shall I make you some mate while we wait?

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler at a gas station in Perito Moreno, and the AI plays your in-laws Ramiro and Elena and their grandson Bruno: keep everyone going with future commitments like llamaré al taller and conseguiremos dónde comer, plus encouragement like ánimo, ya falta poco.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (llamaré al taller cada hora; conseguiremos dónde comer; ánimo, ya falta poco)

examples.es: Iré a la terminal a buscar la encomienda.
examples.en: I'll go to the bus station to pick up the parcel.

examples.es: Mañana a esta hora estaremos otra vez en la ruta.
examples.en: By this time tomorrow we'll be back on the road.

lessons.title: One Delay, Four Listeners: Mechanic to Hotel Desk
lessons.objective: Explain the same delay to a mechanic, a friend, a rental manager and a receptionist, switching register each time.

words.note: Mexico: a signed note confirming a fact, e.g., the repair delay.
Mexico usage; Spain says la reserva.

words.en: Don Armando, I'd like to ask you for a written note about the delay.
words.es: Don Armando, quisiera pedirle una constancia del retraso.
words.note: Formal: usted with the mechanic.

words.en: Would you mind telling me if the part arrives tomorrow?
words.es: ¿Le importaría decirme si la pieza llega mañana?
words.note: Formal softener.

words.en: Hey, here's the thing: the car won't be ready until tomorrow.
words.es: Oye, te cuento: el carro no está listo hasta mañana.
words.note: Informal: tú with your friend.

words.en: Don't worry, I'll let you know as soon as I hear anything.
words.es: No te preocupes, te aviso en cuanto sepa algo.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Mr. Cervera, I'd like to ask you for one more rental day.
words.es: Señor Cervera, quisiera pedirle un día adicional de renta.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would you mind sending me the extension by email?
words.es: ¿Le importaría mandarme la extensión por correo?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Lupita, would it be possible to stay one more night in the same room?
words.es: Lupita, ¿sería posible quedarme una noche más en el mismo cuarto?
words.note: Formal: usted with the receptionist, even by first name.

words.en: Could you confirm the nightly rate for me, please?
words.es: ¿Me podría confirmar la tarifa por noche, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler in Valladolid, and the AI plays mechanic Don Armando, your friend Dana, rental manager Sr. Cervera and receptionist Lupita: explain the same delay to each, switching between usted and tú with softeners like quisiera pedirle, ¿le importaría...? and oye, te cuento.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera pedirle..., ¿le importaría...?, oye, te cuento...)

examples.es: Don Armando, ¿le importaría llamarme cuando llegue la pieza?
examples.en: Don Armando, would you mind calling me when the part arrives?

examples.es: Oye, Dana, te cuento que nos quedamos un día más.
examples.en: Hey, Dana, just so you know, we're staying one more day.

lessons.title: Scooter Skid on Gravel: The Rental Shop's Incident Form
lessons.objective: Narrate a scooter skid in time order and fill in the rental shop's incident form accurately.

words.note: The usual name for a public clinic in Nicaragua.

words.en: the time of the clinic visit

words.note: Standard heading on incident and insurance forms.

words.en: Around 4 we left Moyogalpa for Altagracia.
words.es: A eso de las 4 salimos de Moyogalpa hacia Altagracia.
words.note: A eso de + time = around, approximately.

words.en: We were going slowly, at about 30 kilometers per hour.
words.es: Íbamos despacio, a unos 30 kilómetros por hora.

words.en: After the curve, the scooter slid on the loose gravel.
words.es: Después de la curva, la moto patinó en la grava suelta.

words.en: While he was braking, the rear wheel slid sideways.
words.es: Mientras frenaba, la rueda trasera se fue de lado.
words.note: Mientras + imperfect sets the background action.

words.en: A little later we got to the Altagracia health clinic.
words.es: Al rato llegamos al centro de salud de Altagracia.

words.en: They saw him at 5:20; here is the medical certificate.
words.es: Lo atendieron a las 5:20; aquí está el certificado médico.

words.en: Doña Ileana, what do I put in the description of what happened?
words.es: Doña Ileana, ¿qué pongo en la descripción de los hechos?
words.note: Formal: usted with the shop owner.

words.en: Mateo, do you remember what time they saw you?
words.es: Mateo, ¿te acordás a qué hora te atendieron?
words.note: Informal: Nicaraguan voseo (acordás) between friends.

lessons.speaking: You are filling in the incident form, and the AI is Doña Ileana Duarte, the rental shop owner: narrate Mateo's skid in time order with a eso de, después de la curva, mientras frenaba and al rato, and give the clinic visit time for the insurer.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a eso de las cuatro, al rato, después de la curva, mientras frenaba...)

examples.es: A eso de las 4, mientras bajábamos por el camino de tierra, Mateo frenó.
examples.en: Around 4, while we were going down the dirt road, Mateo braked.

examples.es: Al rato, un señor nos llevó al centro de salud.
examples.en: A little later, a man took us to the health clinic.

lessons.title: Nearly Clipped While Changing a Tire: No-Blame Debrief
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss without blame, say what could have happened, and agree on what changes next time.

words.note: Standard safety term; in conversation people also say casi un accidente.
In Peru la pista means the road or roadway.
Common in Peru for the wheel bolts or lug nuts.
Peruvian word for a gas station.

words.en: The truck nearly hit you, Gonzalo.
words.es: Por poco te da el tráiler, Gonzalo.
words.note: Por poco + present tense describes a past near miss.

words.en: It's nobody's fault; let's talk about what we change.
words.es: No es culpa de nadie; hablemos de qué cambiamos.

words.en: It could have been serious; it passed less than 1 meter away.
words.es: Podría haber sido grave; pasó a menos de 1 metro.

words.en: We almost didn't see it coming around the curve.
words.es: Casi no lo vimos venir por la curva.

words.en: I didn't check where you were either; it's my responsibility too.
words.es: Yo tampoco revisé dónde estabas; también es mi responsabilidad.

words.en: Next time, if we stop at the gas station, we'll be safer.
words.es: La próxima vez, si paramos en el grifo, estaremos más seguros.

words.en: If we work on the passenger side, nobody is exposed.
words.es: Si trabajamos del lado del pasajero, nadie queda expuesto.

words.en: Ms. Patricia, what procedure do you recommend for next time?
words.es: Señora Patricia, ¿qué procedimiento recomienda usted para la próxima vez?
words.note: Formal: usted with the technician.

lessons.speaking: You are debriefing with your companion Gonzalo, and the AI is roadside technician Patricia Huamán: talk through the near miss without blaming anyone, using casi, por poco and podría haber sido, and agree on changes for next time with si paramos..., estaremos...

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco te da el camión; podría haber sido grave; si paramos más lejos, estaremos más seguros)

examples.es: Por poco te da el tráiler cuando sacabas los pernos.
examples.en: The truck nearly hit you while you were taking off the lug nuts.

examples.es: Si ponemos el triángulo más atrás, los camiones nos verán antes.
examples.en: If we put the triangle farther back, the trucks will see us sooner.

lessons.title: Smoke Under the Hood: Emergency Call and Moving Away
lessons.objective: Call emergency services, follow short phone commands, and say what you'll do if the situation changes.

words.note: Mexican word for the car hood.
Mexican word for the car trunk.
Mexico's federal force that patrols the highways.

words.en: Smoke is coming from the hood; we're on Highway 57, heading to San Luis.
words.es: Sale humo del cofre; estamos en la 57, rumbo a San Luis.

words.en: There are 2 of us and nobody is hurt.
words.es: Somos 2 personas y no hay heridos.

words.en: Understood, we won't open the hood and we'll move away.
words.es: Entendido, no abrimos el cofre y nos alejamos.

words.en: If we see flames, we'll move farther away, behind the guardrail.
words.es: Si vemos llamas, nos iremos más lejos, detrás de la barrera.

words.en: If the smoke changes color, I'll tell you right away.
words.es: Si el humo cambia de color, le avisaré enseguida.
words.note: Formal: le with the dispatcher.

words.en: Yes, I'm staying on the line; how long will the fire department take?
words.es: Sí, me quedo en línea; ¿cuánto tardan los bomberos?

words.en: If the National Guard arrives, I'll hand them the phone.
words.es: Si llega la Guardia Nacional, le pasaré el teléfono.

words.en: Renata, don't open the trunk! Things can be replaced.
words.es: Renata, ¡no abras la cajuela! Las cosas se reponen.
words.note: Informal: tú command between companions.

lessons.speaking: You are calling 911, and the AI is the dispatcher: give your location and what is happening, follow short commands like aléjense and no abran el cofre, and say what you'll do if things change with si + present → future (si sale fuego, nos alejaremos más).

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si sale fuego, nos alejaremos más; aléjense, no abran el cofre, quédense en línea)

examples.es: Si el humo aumenta, cruzaremos al otro lado de la barrera.
examples.en: If the smoke increases, we'll cross to the other side of the guardrail.

examples.es: Aléjense del carro y no abran el cofre.
examples.en: Move away from the car and don't open the hood.

lessons.title: Checkpoint Officer Questions Your Temporary Spare
lessons.objective: Answer a traffic officer formally, show documents, and explain how the spare was fitted and checked.

words.note: Everyday Spain name; the formal term is rueda de emergencia.
Spain's term; Latin America says licencia de manejo.
Spain's word for a puncture or flat.
Address her simply as agente.

words.en: Good afternoon, officer. Here is my driver's license.
words.es: Buenas tardes, agente. Aquí tiene mi permiso de conducir.
words.note: Formal: usted throughout with the Guardia Civil.

words.en: Here is the rental contract, which is in my name.
words.es: Aquí tiene el contrato de alquiler, que está a mi nombre.

words.en: The wheel was changed this morning, after a flat.
words.es: La rueda se cambió esta mañana, después de un pinchazo.

words.en: The pressure was checked at a gas station, according to the label.
words.es: Se revisó la presión en una gasolinera, según la etiqueta.

words.en: According to the label, you must not go over 80 km/h.
words.es: Según la etiqueta, no se deben superar los 80 km/h.

words.en: The company was notified and they gave us a case number.
words.es: Se avisó a la empresa y nos dieron un número de expediente.

words.en: Would you like to see the proof of the call on my phone?
words.es: ¿Quiere ver el justificante de la llamada en el móvil?

words.en: We're going straight to the garage the company told us to use.
words.es: Vamos directamente al taller que nos indicó la empresa.

lessons.speaking: You are the driver, and the AI is Guardia Civil agent Lorena Ruiz: answer formally with usted, hand over your license, rental contract and proof of the assistance call, and explain the spare with passive se (se cambió la rueda, se revisó la presión según la etiqueta).

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se cambió la rueda en el arcén, se revisó la presión según la etiqueta, se avisó a la empresa)

examples.es: Se cambió la rueda en el arcén y se pusieron los triángulos.
examples.en: The wheel was changed on the shoulder and the triangles were set out.

examples.es: Se avisó a la empresa de alquiler a las 10:15.
examples.en: The rental company was notified at 10:15.

lessons.title: Write the Breakdown Claim for Your Travel Insurer
lessons.objective: Write a clear claim email with a timeline, costs and receipts, using formal report connectors.

words.note: Insurance term for the covered event, such as a breakdown or accident.
Peru's business tax ID (Registro Único de Contribuyentes); insurers want it on receipts.
In Peru the standard receipt for individuals is a boleta.
Formal written word; in speech people say un recibo a mano.
Formal written word for a sum of money on receipts and claims.
Peru's currency; write S/ before the number.

words.en: Dear Mr. Paredes: I am writing to submit my reimbursement request.
words.es: Estimado señor Paredes: le escribo para presentar mi solicitud de reembolso.
words.note: Formal: a colon, not a comma, after the greeting in Spanish emails.

words.es: En primer lugar, el auto se detuvo a las 14:30.

words.en: Afterwards, the tow truck took us to a garage in Cusco.
words.es: Posteriormente, la grúa nos llevó a un taller en Cusco.

words.en: It should be noted that the tow receipt is handwritten.
words.es: Cabe señalar que el recibo de la grúa está escrito a mano.

words.en: Therefore, I request reimbursement of 450 soles.
words.es: Por lo tanto, solicito el reembolso de 450 soles.

words.en: I am attaching the receipts, the photos and the garage report.
words.es: Adjunto las boletas, las fotos y el informe del taller.

words.en: I will ask the tow operator for a receipt with his tax ID.
words.es: Solicitaré al operador de la grúa un comprobante con su RUC.

words.en: Thank you in advance for your prompt reply.
words.es: Agradezco de antemano su pronta respuesta.
words.note: Formal email closing.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler in a Cusco hotel lobby, and the AI is insurer case handler Ignacio Paredes: write your breakdown claim with a clear timeline, costs and receipts, using en primer lugar, posteriormente, cabe señalar que, por lo tanto and adjunto.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, posteriormente, cabe señalar que, por lo tanto, adjunto)

examples.es: En primer lugar, el motor se apagó en la subida a las 14:30.
examples.en: First, the engine shut off on the climb at 14:30.

examples.es: Cabe señalar que el recibo no tiene RUC; por lo tanto, adjunto una foto de la grúa.
examples.en: It should be noted that the receipt has no tax ID; therefore, I am attaching a photo of the tow truck.

lessons.title: Garage Voice Notes and a Rental Callback
lessons.objective: Handle texts, voice notes and a callback with the garage and rental company to rearrange the plan.

words.note: Colombians say le mando un audio for a WhatsApp voice note.
Colombian word for a courier or freight company.
In Colombia a shipment's tracking number is la guía.
Formal word for extending a rental or a deadline.

words.en: Mr. Yesid, could you confirm whether the part arrives tomorrow?
words.es: Don Yesid, ¿me podría confirmar si la pieza llega mañana?
words.note: Formal: don + first name is respectful and common in Colombia.

words.en: Could you send me the shipping company's tracking number?
words.es: ¿Me podría mandar el número de guía de la transportadora?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I would appreciate it if you let me know as soon as the part arrives.
words.es: Le agradecería que me avisara apenas llegue la pieza.
words.note: Formal: le agradecería que + past subjunctive.

words.en: Sorry, I couldn't answer; I'm returning your call.
words.es: Disculpe, no pude contestar; le devuelvo la llamada.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Paola, I would appreciate it if you sent me the extension in writing.
words.es: Paola, le agradecería que me enviara la prórroga por escrito.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would there be a surcharge if I return the car a day later?
words.es: ¿Habría algún recargo si devuelvo el carro un día después?

words.en: I look forward to your confirmation.
words.note: Formal written closing; a woman writes atenta.

words.en: Can you keep my suitcase until the afternoon, please?
words.es: ¿Me guardas la maleta hasta la tarde, porfa?
words.note: Informal, to hostel staff; porfa is casual for por favor.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler in a Medellín hostel, and the AI is mechanic Yesid Montoya, then rental agent Paola Restrepo: check on the repair by voice note and arrange the rental on the callback, using ¿me podría confirmar...?, le agradecería que... and quedo atento.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿me podría confirmar...?, le agradecería que..., quedo atento, un saludo)

examples.es: ¿Me podría confirmar a qué hora estaría listo el carro?
examples.en: Could you confirm what time the car would be ready?

examples.es: Le agradecería que me mandara la prórroga antes del mediodía.
examples.en: I would appreciate it if you sent me the extension before noon.

lessons.title: Pick-Up Walkthrough and Test Drive with the Advisor
lessons.objective: Walk through the finished repair, test-drive it, and clarify the warranty conditions before paying.

words.note: For a man: el asesor de servicio.
Paraguay and Argentina say la concesionaria for a car dealership.
Break-in period for new pads; ask the advisor what the shop recommends.
Describes a soft brake pedal that sinks too far.

words.en: Before paying, could we take a test drive together?
words.es: Antes de pagar, ¿podríamos dar una vuelta de prueba juntos?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: The pedal isn't spongy anymore; it feels much better.
words.es: El pedal ya no está esponjoso; se siente mucho mejor.

words.en: What would happen if the squeal comes back next week?
words.es: ¿Qué pasaría si vuelve el chirrido la semana que viene?

words.en: Is the warranty valid as long as I go back to an authorized garage?
words.es: ¿La garantía vale siempre que vuelva a un taller autorizado?
words.note: siempre que + subjunctive means as long as.

words.en: Would the warranty be lost if another garage touches the brakes?
words.es: ¿Se perdería la garantía si otro taller toca los frenos?

words.en: So the warranty doesn't cover normal wear, right?
words.es: Entonces la garantía no cubre el desgaste normal, ¿verdad?

words.en: Could you write that on the service order, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo podría anotar en la orden de servicio, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'll pay now, provided you give me the conditions in writing.
words.es: Pago ahora, con tal de que me deje las condiciones por escrito.
words.note: con tal de que always takes the subjunctive.

lessons.speaking: You are picking up your repaired car, and the AI is service advisor Liz Benítez at a dealership in Asunción: go over the brake repair, test-drive it and clarify the warranty before paying, using ¿qué pasaría si...? and siempre que or con tal de que with the subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (¿qué pasaría si vuelve el ruido?; la garantía vale siempre que vuelva a un taller de la red)

examples.es: ¿Qué pasaría si vuelve el ruido en la ruta?
examples.en: What would happen if the noise comes back on the highway?

examples.es: La garantía vale siempre que vuelva a un taller autorizado.
examples.en: The warranty is valid as long as you return to an authorized garage.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Full Breakdown Day in the Picos de Europa
lessons.objective: Lead a full breakdown day: brief, call for help, decide on repairs, refuse unsafe shortcuts, and report it all.

words.note: Spain's usual word for a van.
In Spain a dashboard warning light is un testigo.
Spain, informal: a makeshift repair.
Spain's word for the insurance deductible.
Also called grúa plataforma in Spain.
Charge for a mechanic or tow truck coming out to you.

words.en: Álvaro, Itziar, get out on the right and wait behind the guardrail.
words.es: Álvaro, Itziar, salid por la derecha y esperad tras el guardarraíl.
words.note: Informal, Spain: vosotros commands (salid, esperad) for friends.

words.en: We're at a pull-out on the way up to Covadonga; nobody is hurt.
words.es: Estamos en un apartadero subiendo a Covadonga; nadie está herido.

words.en: We're not opening the expansion tank while it's hot; the manual says so.
words.es: No abrimos el vaso de expansión en caliente; lo dice el manual.

words.en: I'd rather we not drive down; better to load it onto the flatbed.
words.es: Prefiero que no bajemos conduciendo; mejor que la suban a la plataforma.

words.en: If it were the head gasket, how long would the repair take?
words.es: Si fuera la junta de culata, ¿cuánto tardaría la reparación?
words.note: Formal, to the mechanic.

words.en: I authorize the diagnosis as long as you call me before changing anything.
words.es: Autorizo el diagnóstico siempre que me llame antes de cambiar nada.
words.note: Formal; antes de takes nada, not algo.

words.en: Could you confirm whether the replacement van has an excess?
words.es: ¿Me podría confirmar si la furgoneta de sustitución tiene franquicia?
words.note: Formal, to the rental agent.

words.en: Finally, I'm attaching the breakdown report and the photos.
words.es: Por último, adjunto el parte de avería y las fotos.

lessons.speaking: You are leading the group, and the AI plays tow operator Marcos Fidalgo, mechanic Begoña Suárez and the rental agent: brief your friends, call for help, decide on repairs, refuse unsafe shortcuts and report the day, using vosotros commands, si clauses, subjunctive and report connectors.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Si el testigo vuelve a encenderse, pararemos en el primer apartadero.
examples.en: If the warning light comes on again, we'll stop at the first pull-out.

examples.es: Begoña, le agradecería que me llamara antes de cambiar ninguna pieza.
examples.en: Begoña, I would appreciate it if you called me before changing any part.
